item.text: I have enough to synthesize: a declaratory pro-expertise/institution signal from official policy and IAEA engagement, versus concrete 2023 moves that raised risk and were politically driven.

## 1B.7 Research Note: Vladimir Putin, Russia, 2023

**Working judgment:** **Mostly no / weakly negative.** The best pro-expertise evidence is declaratory and institutional on paper, while the year’s concrete nuclear-security moves still favored coercive escalation and widened handling exposure. I found no solid 2023 evidence that Putin materially depoliticized nuclear/security decision-making or replaced loyalist control with independent risk-reducing expertise.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 31.03.2023 г. № 229`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 31 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia’s updated foreign-policy concept says it will strengthen technical and physical nuclear safety, prevent nuclear terrorism, improve predictability, prevent unintentional armed incidents, and support arms control. This is the clearest pro-1B.7 evidence, but it is doctrine, not proof of personnel reform or independent expert control.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.7`, `1B.3`, `1B.4`

- **Title:** `Update 146 – IAEA Director General Statement on Situation in Ukraine`  
  **Publisher:** IAEA  
  **Date:** 13 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/update-146-iaea-director-general-statement-on-situation-in-ukraine](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/update-146-iaea-director-general-statement-on-situation-in-ukraine)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Grossi said he met Rosatom head Alexey Likhachev and an intra-governmental Russian group in Moscow to discuss a nuclear safety and security protection zone around Zaporizhzhya. This shows Russia engaging with institutional and technical channels, which is positive evidence for 1B.7, though still external and crisis-driven rather than an internal change in decision architecture.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.7`, `1B.3`

- **Title:** `Russia suspends participation in New START`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Gulf News  
  **Date:** 21 Feb 2023  
  **URL:** [https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764](https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin announced suspension of Russia’s participation in New START and threatened renewed nuclear testing. That is strong negative evidence for 1B.7 because it reflects a confrontational, leader-driven posture rather than investment in stabilizing institutions or expert-led restraint.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.7`, `1B.4`, `1B.2`

- **Title:** `Russia signs deal to deploy tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus, says they stay under its control`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 25 May 2023  
  **URL:** [https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/](https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia formalized deployment of tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus while saying Moscow would retain control. This points away from expert-risk reduction and toward politically useful forward deployment with expanded handling complexity.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.7`, `1B.3`, `1B.5`, `1B.1`

- **Title:** `Belarus units complete training on Russian tactical nuclear missile systems`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via WSAU / syndicated Reuters report  
  **Date:** 22 Apr 2023  
  **URL:** [https://wsau.com/2023/04/22/belarus-units-complete-training-on-russian-tactical-nuclear-missile-systems/](https://wsau.com/2023/04/22/belarus-units-complete-training-on-russian-tactical-nuclear-missile-systems/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Belarusian units trained in Russia on the Iskander system and tactical nuclear warhead handling. This widens the number of personnel and institutions involved in nuclear-capable operations, which cuts against a strong 1B.7 reading.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.7`, `1B.3`, `1B.6`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2023 evidence that Putin made a concrete personnel or governance shift toward independent nuclear/security expertise, such as sidelining ideologues, reducing loyalist control, or creating stronger internal checks on nuclear decisions. The best positive evidence is limited to doctrine and IAEA-linked consultations; the concrete 2023 record still looks politicized and risk-increasing.

### Bottom line

**Mostly no.** Putin’s 2023 public policy language favored safety and institutions, but his actual nuclear/security behavior centered on confrontation, New START suspension, and Belarus deployment, not clear investment in expert-led risk reduction.
